steps.what: Choose the biological question and check relevant teaching examples
Initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussion

tasks.design: Retain the teacher's question choice and live moderation, using the current {DOCS} examples. No written discussion report or automated student evaluation is introduced; a native question bank does not remove the teacher's contextual selection in this boundary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Productive discussion depends on the students' actual reasoning and misunderstandings.
tasks.enabler_now: No established software change replaces that interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Drawing out quiet students and challenging biological misconceptions fairly.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room and adapt follow-up questions.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: classroom discussion facilitation requires contextual human interaction.

assumptions: Boundary is question selection and live discussion, not grading or attendance recording. Shares are provisional.
The teacher obtains objectives and examples from existing teaching sources in s1; students produce contributions during s2. No structured discussion transcript is assumed.

Lookups are explicit in s1. No first report, record write or send is established for this discussion; actual participation grading belongs in its own observed assessment workflow. Do not invent a discussion log.
Native question access is already present and no removed work is established. No change means zero upkeep.
unknowns: Whether actual written discussion prompts or participation records are required
research_questions: Does the discussion task create an actual artefact beyond the selected question?

already_counted.description: Question selection and live moderation remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All focal work remains. A discussion with major misconceptions still needs full moderation; no automated assessment or invented report supplies a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check laboratory protocol, hazards and equipment readiness
Supervise student laboratory technique and intervene in unsafe or incorrect work

tasks.design: Retain protocol checking and direct laboratory supervision. The existing {DOCS} protocol is already available; no camera, remote supervisor replacement or new monitoring register is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unsafe technique and unexpected biological results require immediate contextual intervention.
tasks.enabler_now: No established software change removes that supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Watching several students safely and explaining technique errors.
tasks.human_edge: Notice developing hazards and intervene before harm.
tasks.altitude: Unchanged laboratory supervision and safety responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: hands-on laboratory supervision and safety intervention remain human work.

assumptions: Boundary is supervision, not students' own experimental labour or formal grading. Provisional shares are not measured.
The laboratory coordinator supplies the approved protocol and hazard information; the teacher checks them in s1. No new structured sensor or student-performance feed is assumed.

Required record work must be identified separately: actual attendance and grade records are owned by task 5805, not duplicated here. A safety incident report, if triggered, needs its own real first write and release; do not invent a routine post-lab log.
Test native protocol access first; the current copy is already available and no navigation saving is established. No proposed change means zero upkeep.
research_questions: Which actual safety or competence entries are required in addition to supervision?

already_counted.description: Protocol checks and direct supervision remain in full.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All focal work remains. Hazardous or unfamiliar exercises retain full supervision; no student labour or unrequired record is converted into teacher savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Find current biological literature and relevant professional conferences
Read and critically assess current biological literature
Participate in professional conferences and question presented findings

tasks.design: Configure saved topic searches in the scholarly literature-database category {OTHER} to avoid re-entering stable biological search terms. Keep relevance screening, critical reading, colleague discussion and conference participation human; no automatic scientific summary substitutes for the sources.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated searches consume effort, but field developments still need scientific appraisal.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved searches reuse stable terms and filters.
tasks.still_hard: Separating robust findings from preliminary or conflicting evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Judge methods and implications for research and teaching.
tasks.altitude: Less search setup; unchanged responsibility to read and evaluate.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: scholarly database saved searches can reuse stable topic terms and filters while relevance and scientific appraisal stay human.

assumptions: Boundary includes literature discovery, reading, colleague exchange and conference participation. Shares are hypotheses; event booking and travel are not hidden as savings.

The teacher creates and verifies topic terms and filters within retained s1; publishers and conference organisers supply original metadata and programmes. No new structured extraction or free bibliography is assumed.
Test native saved searches first. Only repeated term/filter entry, 30% of s1, is removed. New topics, screening and conference discovery stay in its retained 70%.
No required written current-awareness report is established. Personal notes, if actually kept, require their own entry time before estimating a note benefit; no trailing summary log is invented.
research_questions: Do saved searches remove repeated setup while retaining discovery of emerging biological topics?

already_counted.description: Query revision and relevance screening remain in s1.

incremental.description: Teacher refreshes saved search terms after changes in field terminology.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 15*0.30=4.5 query-setup hours removed less 1 upkeep gives 3.5 net. Cautious case: a newly emerging subfield needs mostly fresh terms, leaving 1.2 hours of known-topic setup removed and 0.2 net; reading and professional exchange remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain attendance, grades and required student records

steps.what: Establish actual student attendance and resolve identity uncertainties
Enter original attendance and required course-record facts
Enter examiner-confirmed grades in the course gradebook
Check final grade-transfer snapshot, student matches and target course registry
outputs: checked grade-transfer snapshot and registry destination

steps.what: Re-enter checked grades into the separate official student registry
inputs: checked grade-transfer snapshot and registry destination

steps.what: Calculate required attendance and grade totals for record reconciliation
Reconcile imported results and check final official release payload and students
inputs: checked grade-transfer snapshot and registry destination
outputs: final reconciled result-release payload and students

steps.what: Release the reconciled official results to the matching students
inputs: final reconciled result-release payload and students

tasks.design: Test the native {LMS} export and student-registry category {OTHER} import before custom integration, transferring only the checked grade snapshot and generating native reconciliation totals. Keep original attendance capture, original confirmed-grade entry and all matching/repair human; official result release follows reconciliation of the imported final payload.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course grades may require a second entry into an official registry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native export/import and grouped totals can remove true second-system retyping and manual tallying.
tasks.still_hard: Correct student, course, assessment attempt and grade-scale matching.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve disputed or exceptional records and protect official result integrity.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate entry and arithmetic, with the same record and release responsibility.

evidence.claim: Radboud guidance says Brightspace grades must also be published in OSIRIS, documenting a second-system grade-record requirement; local manual effort still needs confirmation.

assumptions: Boundary is maintaining existing attendance and grades, including a separate official registry where required. Shares are provisional, not a measured institution baseline. Marking and grade decisions belong to assessment tasks and earn no saving here.

The teacher verifies attendance in s1 and captures it in s2. Appointed examiners supply confirmed student identifier, course, assessment, attempt, grade, scale and date; the teacher captures original grades in s3. Administration supplies course/registry mapping. No free structured first capture is assumed.

Test native export/import and totals first. s4 creates/checks the exact transfer snapshot. Wrong mappings, unsupported grades and failed imports stop for manual repair within retained s4/s7; original entries and ordinary saves s2-s3 remain fully retained and ungated.

s5 removes only real re-entry into a second system, not a same-system save. s6 removes actual manual totals, not existing automatic runtime. Verify both exist locally; if already automated remove their labour benefit.

s4 binds the exact registry transfer, including student/course/attempt mapping, before s5; s7 separately checks the complete imported final release and matching students before s8. Edits void approval. The teacher must already have actual import/release authority; otherwise add the real authorised actor and positive labour.
research_questions: Can a native draft import preserve student, assessment attempt and grade scale and reconcile before release?

already_counted.description: Original captures, matching checks, failed-import repair and final reconciliation remain.

incremental.description: Teacher checks mappings and totals after course or grading-scale changes.

approvals.approved_version: s4 final checked grade-transfer snapshot, student/course/attempt mappings and exact target registry; edits void approval
s7 final reconciled imported result payload and exact matching student destinations; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 25 second-entry hours and 10 tally hours removed less 2 upkeep gives 33 net. Cautious case: legacy attempt codes force most grades through manual entry, leaving 5 hours of supported imports and 2 hours of supported totals removed, or 5 net; first capture and repair stay counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Native grade transfers and totals can reduce duplicate records work; discussion, laboratory supervision and scientific appraisal remain human.
role.ambitious_version: No automated learning-outcome decisions or reduced laboratory supervision are proposed.
